newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FAI Life says sees strong future.
newsitem.headline: FAI Life says sees strong future.

text.p: FAI Life Ltd chairman Malcolm Irving said on Friday that the company was well placed for strong long-term performance.
"The board considers the company is well positioned for strong long-term performance," Irving said in a statement.
Earlier, the company announced a 37 percent jump in annual net profit to A$11.20 million. It will pay a fully franked final dividend of three cents, up from 2.5 cents previously.
"The ability of the company to pay fully franked dividends in the future will be dependent upon operational and trading activities," Irving said.

Regular premium income rose to A$100.9 million during the 1995/96 year from A$88.75 million previously. Irving said that while there was a fall in single premium product sales, income overall increased to A$192.5 million from A$169.1 million. Investment performance improved significantly during the year with investment revenue recording a A$62.6 million turnaround.
Total assets grew 19 percent to A$560 million.
At 1.00 p.m. (0500 GMT), FAI Life shares were steady at 87 cents. FAI Life is about 42 percent owned by FAI Insurances Ltd .
